children: CIMB's 3Q earnings are expected to have been fairly resilient despite volatility in Indonesia and debt markets, supported by robust loan growth, and rising treasury and wealth management income, Maybank IB analyst Desmond Ch'ng says in a note. However, expected interest rate hikes in Indonesia and a weaker rupiah could pressure lending margins and earnings into 2027, he reckons. CIMB may also explore taking its Indonesian subsidiary, CIMB Niaga, private amid market volatility, he notes. Ch'ng cuts CIMB's 2027-2028 earnings estimates by 1%-2%, to factor in expected rupiah weakness. Maybank cuts CIMB's target price to 7.40 ringgit from 8.40 ringgit, while maintaining a hold rating. Shares are 0.6% higher at 7.19 ringgit.(yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
